pair:room-topology · no-progress signatu: ═══ HEIGHT PAID 2026-08-17 · §PR-09-WALLSIG-HEIGHT · BASELINE-Y STILL OPEN ══════
The founder RULED on the HEIGHT half of this finding, and it is now closed in code:
'YES — include canonical wall height in _computeWallSig, since a height change is
a geometric identity change.'  CAVEAT: 'use the canonical/normalized wall height
— NOT a derived value that can fluctuate because of representation or
floating-point noise.'
`_computeWallSig` now folds `WallData.height` through the SAME `mm()` quantiser the
baseline coordinates and thickness already use — Math.round(metres * 1000), INTEGER
millimetres — appended as `^<mm>`:
so the A8 detail line now reads `height-only edit changes it: true`. Integer-mm
quantisation is what honours the caveat: two doubles differing only in their last bits
(3 vs 0.1+0.2+2.7) produce the SAME token, while a real 1 mm authoring change does not.
The value is read off the required, authored, metres-valued store field
(WallTypes.ts:258) and is never re-derived from a level, a slab offset, a rake
projection or a built mesh.
Both directions are pinned in packages/room-topology/src/__tests__/
roomRedetectNoProgressGuard.test.ts §PR-09-WALLSIG-HEIGHT, watched RED first (3 of the
5 new cases failed before the change): a height-only edit MUST invalidate; float noise,
a `properties` patch and a `materialId` change MUST NOT. The over-invalidation direction
is not decoration — this signature feeds the no-progress gate AND the circuit breaker,
which exist to STOP runaway redetect loops, so a field that flickers is as harmful as a
field that is missing.
⚠ THE ARM A8 COMPARATOR WAS NOT ISOLATED, AND THE HEIGHT FIX EXPOSED IT. On the first
run after height landed, A8 went GREEN — `height-only edit changes it: true; baseline-y-
only edit changes it: true` — and the gate printed [3] STALE LEDGER demanding the finding
be struck. It was an ARTEFACT. A8 measured `afterY !== base` and `afterThickness !== base`,
i.e. every probe against the ORIGINAL signature rather than against the one immediately
before its own edit — and the height edit is still applied when the y probe runs. So the
moment height entered the signature, y and thickness read `true` FOR FREE. The printed
signature `n1|w_9:0,0>5000,0#200^3000` contains no y term at all, which is how the artefact
was caught: the number disagreed with the string beside it. Had the entry been struck on
that reading, a NAMED, still-live divergence would have left the ledger and the gate would
have been permanently green on a claim that is false.
FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT, tightened and never loosened: each probe is now compared with
the signature taken immediately BEFORE its own edit (heightCovered = afterHeight !== base,
yCovered = afterY !== afterHeight, thicknessCovered = afterThickness !== afterY). This can
only turn a reading from true to false. No floor moved, no threshold moved, and the five
in-run controls are untouched. Re-measured: `height-only edit changes it: true;
baseline-y-only edit changes it: false; thickness edit changes it: true` — 8 pairs
exercised, 5/5 controls proven, 1 finding, exit 1 DECLARED-LEVEL, exactly as before.
THE ENTRY STAYS ON THE LEDGER because arm A8 is a CONJUNCTION over height AND baseline
`y`, and `y` was NOT ruled on. It is deliberately NOT bundled into the height ruling:
· a wall's AUTHORED vertical placement is `baseOffset` — worldY = level.elevation +
slabBaseOffset + baseOffset (SlabWallCoupling.ts:61) — and `baseOffset` is read by
NEITHER `_computeWallSig` NOR `_wallGeometryChanged`. This gate never drives it.
· `baseLine[*].y` is documented by WallTypes.ts §WALL-AUDIT-2026-M7 as a world-space
MIRROR of `level.elevation` that goes STALE when a level's elevation changes, and
which the WallFragmentBuilder re-projects away at render time — verbatim, 'only the
persisted DTO value is misleading'. Migration to relative `y === 0` is an open,
deliberately deferred item.
Adding `y` would turn the arm green while encoding the field its own canonical-convention
note calls misleading, and would leave the field that actually carries elevation still
unmeasured. That is a SECOND ruling with its own caveat, so it is REPORTED, not taken.
The declared level is UNCHANGED at 1 — to be lowered when the y/baseOffset question is
decided, never raised.
═══ THE ORIGINAL MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-12 — the height half is superseded above ═══
MEASURED 2026-08-12. `RoomTopologyObserver._computeWallSig` (RoomTopologyObserver.ts:566-584)
builds its per-level no-progress signature from id + baseline X/Z + thickness:
`height` is ABSENT, and baseline `y` is ABSENT. Both trackers, by contrast, treat
height AND y as geometry-changing (DoorDependencyTracker.ts:112-119 and the window
twin at :93-101) and re-anchor every hosted opening for them — arm A3 proves the
cascade fires for a height-only edit.
CONSEQUENCE: an edit that one half of the propagation spine treats as a real move is,
to the other half, byte-identical geometry. A height-only or y-only wall edit therefore
(a) is DROPPED by the committed-path no-progress gate when a redetect has already run
over that signature (RoomTopologyObserver.ts:254-258), and
(b) counts as a same-signature repeat toward the execution circuit-breaker (:525-539),
so six such edits inside one second suppress redetection until the X/Z geometry
changes.
The `add`/`update`/`remove` WallStore subscription still schedules through the debounce
path, which is why this is a MASKING risk rather than a total loss — and it is exactly
the class of defect that only shows up on a specific interaction ordering.
NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY [2026-08-12 — the height clause of this paragraph is now
ANSWERED; see the PR-09 block at the top. The `y` clause still stands]. Whether wall
height belongs in the signature is a decision, not a typo: room detection is a
2D-footprint function, so height arguably does not affect the room polygon — but
baseline `y` moves the wall vertically and room VOLUME/finish surfaces do follow wall
height. Making the call belongs with the C71 topology gates, and
`packages/room-topology/` is another agent's territory.
